title: feat(chatbot): report status to OpAMP server
author: cijothomas
body:
Wires the chatbot service (Python) to report its status to the demo's OpAMP server using the OpenTelemetry Python OpAMP client, so a Python SDK-instrumented app appears in the OpAMP UI alongside the Collector, cart service (.NET), and product-catalog service (Go).

Follows the same pattern as the cart and product-catalog service OpAMP support. Enabled only with the agentic and observability stacks.

Note: the current Python OpAMP client provides the agent loop and message helpers, but does not yet include WebSocket transport or health reporting helpers. This PR keeps those pieces local to the demo so the chatbot can report to the demo OpAMP server/UI in the same way as the .NET and Go services.

Question for maintainers: should we include this Python example now to show another SDK language reporting to OpAMP, or hold off until the Python OpAMP client has built-in WebSocket and health reporting support so the demo code can stay smaller?

comments.author: ps48
comments.text:
> Question for maintainers: should we include this Python example now to show another SDK language reporting to OpAMP, or hold off until the Python OpAMP client has built-in WebSocket and health reporting support so the demo code can stay smaller?

Yes, I think shipping this now is fine showing another SDK language reporting to OpAMP has value, and we already do this for the C# cart service. But let's open an upstream issue (this is a pre-req convention that we follow for missing pieces in upstream) on `opentelemetry-opamp-client` for built-in WebSocket + health reporting, and link it here, so this demo glue has a clear removal path once the library supports it natively.
